A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Vision-LSTM and retain its alternating mLSTM backbone. The main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A and B are readable and support matching retained, revised and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet-1K training results, architecture and pooling ablations, long-sequence fine-tuning, training-duration experiments and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 reports original ImageNet-1K, ADE20K and VTAB-1K results, architectural ablations, robustness evaluations and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The alternating mLSTM backbone remains. v3 Section 4.1 specifies replacing the causal 1D query/key convolution with a 3x3 2D convolution, while Figure 2 and Section 4.2 adopt bilateral concatenation instead of v1's default averaging. These are localized component changes; concatenation was already tested in v1.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates ImageNet classification. v3 adds ADE20K semantic segmentation, all 19 VTAB-1K datasets covering natural, medical, satellite and structured tasks, and ImageNet-C/A/R/Sketch evaluations. These substantially broaden task requirements, domains and test conditions.

E2.justification: The ImageNet comparison in Table 1 adds VRWKV and Mamba-R, replaces the earlier ConvNeXt variants with isotropic small/base variants, and removes ViT-B384 and S4ND comparisons. DeiT-family and Vim comparators remain. Mamba-R was only discussed and cited in v1, whereas v3 reports its comparison scores.

E3.justification: Main ViL training changes from 224-resolution training to 192-resolution pre-training followed by 224-resolution fine-tuning. v3 Tables 1 and 10 specify 20 fine-tuning epochs for tiny/small and five for base, although Section 3 generically states 20. Traversal ablations change from 400 epochs on 100 classes at resolution 128 to 100 epochs on full ImageNet-1K at 224. v3 also introduces downstream evaluation protocols and revised FLOP accounting; the overlapping-patch long-sequence protocol is removed.

E4.justification: v3 expands design testing to query/key convolutions, positional embeddings, oct-directional traversal and controlled sequential-versus-parallel blocks, with segmentation outcomes alongside classification. Pooling studies are revised, while v1's explicit parameter-sharing comparisons disappear. Appendix A adds corruption/domain-shift tests and extends the retained training-duration analysis to ADE20K and VTAB.

E5.justification: v1 provides no repeated-run or seed protocol. For the new VTAB experiments, v3 specifies five seeds per candidate learning rate and five final training runs, reporting mean test accuracy (Section 3.3 and Appendix B.4). No dispersion estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces ViL-T/S/B accuracies of 77.3/80.7/81.6 with 78.3/81.5/82.4 under changed architecture and training, so these are not same-setting gains. v3 adds extensive downstream and robustness results, including ViL-B's 48.6 single-scale ADE20K mIoU and 70.9 VTAB average accuracy. The T+/S+ and long-sequence result entries disappear. Appendix A.1 retains the original runtime values.

T1.justification: v3 Section 2.2 adds mode-specific complexity reasoning, distinguishing recurrent, quadratic parallel and chunkwise computation and deriving the chunkwise cost O(TSd + (T/S)d^2). v1 only asserts linear scaling. The additional recurrence equations mainly formalize the inherited mLSTM; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The generic-backbone proposal and alternating-block contribution remain. However, v3's abstract, contribution list and conclusion explicitly extend the main performance claims to transfer classification and segmentation and add a favorable pre-training cost-to-performance claim. v1's concrete superiority claims principally concern ImageNet classification.

C2.justification: v3 interprets strong downstream performance despite weaker base-scale ImageNet accuracy and discusses classification-versus-segmentation tradeoffs in pooling. It replaces v1's center-bias rationale for averaging with a concatenation-based choice. Section 5 substantially expands limitations, explicitly acknowledging slower execution than ViTs, the limitations of FLOPs as a runtime proxy and dependence on future optimized kernels.

D1.justification: v3 adds detailed VTAB and ADE20K fine-tuning specifications, including learning-rate searches, layer grouping, segmentation heads, augmentation and multiscale evaluation. It newly documents precision and autocast settings for retained training pipelines and explains FLOP counting and CUDA-operation handling. Appendix B.1 revises the hardware description and estimated project compute from 25K to 38K A100 GPU-hours. The project-page access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds a substantial Related Work section covering CNN feature learning, backbone development, self-supervised pre-training and sequence models in vision. New discussions and citations include RWKV/VRWKV, VideoMamba, U-Mamba and hardware-efficient linear attention. This broadens research positioning beyond v1's primarily introductory comparison with transformers and vision SSMs.

P1.justification: v3 reorganizes the short report into a fuller narrative with mathematical preliminaries, task-specific experiment subsections, a separate ablation section, dedicated limitations and related work, and an explicit contribution list. The method explanation, pooling discussion and conclusion are substantially developed or rewritten, although portions of the introduction remain.

P2.justification: v3 adds performance/compute plots in Figures 1 and 3 and redraws the traversal illustration to include eight directions. Table 1 gains epoch and FLOP columns and a new structure; ablations become grouped subtables, and downstream, robustness and implementation tables are added. The original architecture schematic is retained as Figure 2 with an expanded, revised caption.

improvement.justification: v1's generic-backbone claim rests principally on ImageNet classification. v3 substantially strengthens that claim through dense prediction, transfer across 19 datasets and robustness tests (Tables 2, 3 and 9). Cross-task ablations, detailed downstream protocols and clearer runtime limitations improve the paper's evidential strength and reproducibility. Although long-sequence comparisons are removed and projected speed advantages over ViTs remain unverified, the broader validation resolves an important deficiency in the original paper.
